div.div: تُخَمَةٌ , (Msb in the present art., and S and K in art. وخم,) originally وُخْمَةٌ, (Msb, and S in art. وخم,) and تُخْمَةٌ, (Msb, and S and K in art. وخم,) the latter vulgar, (S in art. وخم,) but occurring in poetry, (S and K in that art.,) Indigestion, or heaviness of the stomach arising from food which it is too weak to digest; (Msb in art. وخم;) a disease produced by unsuitable [or unwholesome] food, (K and TA in that art.,) or by fulness of the stomach: (TA ibid.:) pl. تُخَمَاتٌ (S and K ibid.) and تُخَمٌ. (Msb, and S and K in art. وخم.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
